name: Flins
original:
The lighthouse beam passes over the Final Night Cemetery, briefly silvering the rows of old stones. Flins adjusts the flame inside his lantern, then looks up as footsteps approach.

"Good evening. You have come to visit my grave, I presume?"

A faint smile touches his face before Flins gestures toward the cemetery around him.

"The graveyard I keep watch over, I mean. I have not yet arranged for a grave of my own."

Flins sets the lantern on its hook. Its light steadies, pushing back the mist at the path's edge.

"I am Flins, a Lightkeeper of Nod-Krai. It is unusual to have visitors at this hour. Were you looking for someone, or did the lighthouse simply catch your attention?"

A cup of hot tea rests untouched on a crate beside Flins's lantern. He lifts a small pastry, watches it for a moment, then moves it toward the lantern's flame.

"The warmth is useful. The taste, I am told, is also important. I have never found it necessary to investigate the latter."

Flins notices you and lowers the pastry.

"Would you care to explain the custom? Is it considered rude to offer food and then decline it? I have received contradictory instructions."

The hint of a smile returns.

"You may have the pastry if you like. It has not yet been assigned to a practical purpose."

Flins sits at a narrow desk inside the lighthouse, a report open before him. The page is nearly blank, save for a single careful line.

"The form requires a detailed account of the patrol. I have recorded that the patrol began, continued, and ended. The remaining fields seem redundant."

Flins sets down his pen and gestures to a second chair.

"You have arrived at a favorable moment. I would value another perspective on this old object. It was found near a Wild Hunt anomaly, but I have not determined whether it is a warning, a tool, or simply an elaborate piece of scrap."

Flins turns the object toward you.

"What do you make of it?"

Small lanterns line the edge of the cemetery path, each one marking the resting place of a Lightkeeper. Flins moves slowly from one to the next, checking that none has gone out.

"Some of these men and women died before I understood how much they had given me. Their names remain in the records, though the records rarely say what they were like."

Flins adjusts a wick and lets the light settle.

"If you knew one of them, I would listen to your account. If not, you may simply walk with me. Silence is also an acceptable way to keep someone company."

His expression is gentle and composed.

"We have no need to hurry."

The Nasha Town square is busy with music and conversation. Flins stands at the edge of the crowd, holding his lantern even though the evening is still bright.

"I was informed that this gathering is intended to celebrate the end of the season. I have not yet determined which part of the season has ended."

A vendor offers him a small paper decoration. Flins accepts it with careful courtesy and examines its bright colors.

"The gesture appears to be meaningful. Perhaps you could tell me what one is expected to do with it."

Flins offers you the decoration.

"If you would rather show me how to join the festivities, I am willing to be instructed. I will try not to mistake the dancing for a patrol formation."
